newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - BTP vols fade but deals still plentiful.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - BTP vols fade but deals still plentiful.

text.p: Implied volatility of options on Italian bond futures slipped on Monday as last week's roaring gains in the underlying futures market petered out, traders and brokers said.

But they said there was plenty of activity in both exchange-traded and over-the-counter (OTC) markets. In the OTC market, investors were gearing their strategies towards interest rate cuts by the end of the year, they said.
"Vol is drifting down a bit," said an options broker at a French investment house in London. "A degree of stability appears to have returned."

The broker quoted implied volatility of the December 121.50 stradle at around 7.4 percent in early afternoon, slightly lower than Friday. LIFFE's data shows volatility of 122.00 calls and puts at 7.68 percent on Friday.
December BTP futures on LIFFE were quoted at 121.52 at 1255 GMT, down 38 basis points from Friday.

Italian bond futures soared more than four full points last week to a new all-time high of 122.50 as euphoria over the government's deficit-slashing 1997 budget swept the market and raised speculation interest rates would soon be cut.
Brokers said volumes at LIFFE ranged throughout the strikes in both calls and puts.

The broker at the French house noted a German securities institution bought 500 lots of 125.00 December calls at around 7.25 percent volatility. "They weren't doing it as a vol trade they were just doing it straight," he said.
LIFFE screens showed the December 122.00 strike with the biggest volume of calls at 662 lots.

Among puts, he said the 119.00-116.00 put spread was traded. He added locals were busy with a put butterfly, consisting of 500 lots of 118.00 puts, 1,000 lots of 116.50 puts and 500 lots of 114.50 puts.
An OTC options broker at an Italian bank in London said investors expected volatility of options on the three-year area of the curve to hold steady but drift lower on other maturities.
"There's a lot of interest to buy volatility in the three-year because people are expecting a cut from the Bank of Italy next month," he said.
"Volatility in the three-year area of the curve should stay at 17 to 18 percent," he said.
He said investors had already begun to develop strategies for waning volitity into the end of the year, but rising into next.
"We have seen market-makers selling short-term volatility and buying volatility over the six month to one-year (area) to be long for the next year," he said.
